The fix is straightforward — the final queryset joins on product types via an OR of two many-to-many relations, which can produce duplicate attribute rows. Adding `.distinct()` deduplicates.

Done. 

The bug: in `filter_attributes_by_product_types`, the final filter joins attributes across two many-to-many relations (`product_types` and `product_variant_types`) against a set of product type IDs. When multiple product types in the category/collection reference the same attribute, the SQL join produces one row per matching product type, so the same attribute appears multiple times in the result.

The fix appends `.distinct()` to that queryset, so each attribute is returned exactly once while still being included if referenced by any matching product type. Because this is the shared implementation, the deduplication now applies to both the legacy `filter` path (`AttributeFilter`) and the newer `where` path (`AttributeWhere`), for both `inCategory` and `inCollection`.
